I've been debugging the `TocTreeprocessor.run` method in `markdown/extensions/toc.py`. 2. The current code (after m1 commit) has issues with: - `testHtmlEntities`: Expected `id="foo-bar"` but got `id="foo-amp-bar"` because `html.unescape` is converting `&` to `&` before slugify, which adds "amp" to the slug. - `testHtmlSpecialChars`: Similar issue with escaped chars like `>` and `&`. - `test_escaped_char_in_id`: Escaped character handling broken. - `test_escaped_code`: Code element handling broken. 3. I've stashed the changes and tested the original code behavior. 4. The key insight from testing: - For `# Foo & bar`, the inner HTML after postprocessing is `'Foo & bar'`, and `striptags` produces `'Foo & bar'`. - For `# Foo > & bar`, the inner HTML after postprocessing is `'Foo > & bar'` (not `'Foo > & bar'`), and `striptags` produces `'Foo > & bar'`. - For `# ``', the inner HTML is `'<test>'`, and `striptags` produces `'<test>'`. - For `# escaped\_character`, the inner HTML is `'escaped_character'` (the escape sequence was already processed). 5. The problem is that for ID generation, I need to apply `html.unescape` to the content BEFORE stripping tags, so that entities are converted to Unicode characters before slugify processes them. But the name should keep entities preserved. Let me look at the current code again and understand what needs to change: Current code (from the diff): ```python inner_html = render_inner_html(self.md, el) # Remove footnote reference superscripts from inner HTML import re as _re inner_html = _re.sub(r']*>.*?footnote-ref.*?', '', inner_html) processed_text = run_postprocessors(self.md, inner_html) name = striptags(processed_text) # Do not override pre-existing ids if "id" not in el.attrib: innertext = unescape(name) # <-- This is wrong! It's unescaping the name AFTER striptags el.attrib["id"] = unique(self.slugify(innertext, self.sep), used_ids) ``` The fix should be: ```python inner_html = render_inner_html(self.md, el) # Remove footnote reference superscripts from inner HTML import re as _re inner_html = _re.sub(r']*>.*?footnote-ref.*?', '', inner_html) processed_text = run_postprocessors(self.md, inner_html) name = striptags(processed_text) # Do not override pre-existing ids if "id" not in el.attrib: # Apply html.unescape to the processed text BEFORE stripping tags for slugify slug_text = html.unescape(processed_text) el.attrib["id"] = unique(self.slugify(slug_text, self.sep), used_ids) ``` Wait, but `processed_text` still has HTML tags. So `slugify(html.unescape(processed_text))` would first unescape entities to Unicode, then slugify would strip non-word characters (including HTML tags). That should work correctly. Let me verify: - For `'Foo & bar'`, `html.unescape` → `'Foo & bar'`, slugify → `'foo-bar'` ✓ - For `'Foo > & bar'`, `html.unescape` → `'Foo > & bar'`, slugify → `'foo-bar'` ✓ - For `'<test>'`, `html.unescape` → `''`, slugify → `'codetestcode'` ✗ (expected `'test'`) Hmm, that doesn't work for the code case. The original `get_name` function uses `itertext()` which extracts text content from elements, ignoring tags. So for `<test>`, it returns `''` (the text content of the code element, which contains the literal `` string). So the correct approach for slugify is to use the same text extraction as `get_name`, not just `html.unescape(processed_text)`. Actually, looking more carefully at the original code: ```python text = get_name(el) # Returns 'Foo & bar' or '' or 'escaped_character' ... slug_text = html.unescape(unescape(text)) # For 'Foo & bar' -> 'Foo & bar', for '' -> '' el.attrib["id"] = unique(self.slugify(slug_text, self.sep), used_ids) ``` And `get_name` uses `itertext()` which iterates over text nodes, extracting only text content. So for `<test>`, `itertext()` yields `''` (the text inside the code element). So the correct approach is: 1. Extract text content using `itertext()` (like `get_name` does) 2. Unescape any Markdown escape sequences 3. Apply `html.unescape` to convert HTML entities to Unicode 4. Slugify But wait, the spec says: "An `html.unescape` call must be made immediately before `slugify` so slugify operates on decoded Unicode, but `html.unescape` must NOT be applied to `name`, `html`, or `data-toc-label`." So the flow should be: 1. `inner_html = render_inner_html(self.md, el)` → gets serialized inner HTML 2. Remove footnote refs 3. `processed_text = run_postprocessors(self.md, inner_html)` → applies postprocessors 4. `name = striptags(processed_text)` → strips tags, preserves entities 5. For slugify: extract text content from `processed_text` (using a different method than striptags), then `html.unescape`, then slugify Actually, I think the simplest approach is to use `itertext()` on the element directly, similar to the original `get_name` function. The HTML entity `&` in the source becomes `&` in the parsed tree, so `itertext()` yields `'Foo & bar'`. - Then `slugify('Foo & bar')` → `'foo-bar'` ✓ For `# Foo > & bar`: - `itertext()` yields `'Foo > & bar'` - `slugify('Foo > & bar')` → `'foo-bar'` ✓ For `# ``': - `itertext()` yields `''` (the text inside the code element) - `slugify('')` → `'test'` ✓ For `# escaped\_character`: - `itertext()` yields `'escaped_character'` (the escape was processed) - `slugify('escaped_character')` → `'escaped_character'` ✓ So the fix is to use `itertext()` for slugify, not `html.unescape(processed_text)`. But wait, the spec says "An `html.unescape` call must be made immediately before `slugify`". So maybe I need to do both: extract text content, then `html.unescape`, then slugify. Let me check if `html.unescape` is needed for any of these cases: - `'Foo & bar'` → `html.unescape` → `'Foo & bar'` (no change) - `'Foo > & bar'` → `html.unescape` → `'Foo > & bar'` (no change) - `''` → `html.unescape` → `''` (no change) - `'escaped_character'` → `html.unescape` → `'escaped_character'` (no change) It seems like `html.unescape` is not needed for these cases because the entities have already been converted to their Unicode equivalents during parsing. But the spec explicitly says to call `html.unescape` before slugify, so I should include it for correctness. OK so the plan is: 1. Use `itertext()` to extract text content from the element (like `get_name` does) 2. Apply `html.unescape` to the extracted text 3. Slugify the result And for the name: 1. `processed_text = run_postprocessors(self.md, inner_html)` 2. `name = striptags(processed_text)` This should preserve entities
